weather.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 9 at 1:12PM MDT until October 11 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
weather.area: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Tooele and Rush Valleys; Eastern Box Elder County; Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Utah Valley; Cache Valley/Utah Portion; Wasatch Back; Bear Lake and Bear River Valley; Sanpete Valley
weather.text:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...The Wasatch Front, Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Cache Valley/Utah Portion, Wasatch Back,
Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, and Sanpete Valley.

* WHEN...From 3 AM Saturday to 6 AM MDT Sunday. Winds will initially
start off Saturday morning as southwesterly downslope off favored
terrain, such as the Oquirrhs, before becoming more widespread in
the late morning to early afternoon hours.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.
weather.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles and vehicles with trailers. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 1:04PM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
weather.area: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Tooele and Rush Valleys; Eastern Box Elder County; Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Utah Valley; Cache Valley/Utah Portion; Wasatch Back; Bear Lake and Bear River Valley; Wasatch Mountains I-80 North; Wasatch Mountains South of I-80; Western Uinta Mountains; Western Uinta Basin; Western Millard and Juab Counties
weather.text:
Moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel will
impact Utah this weekend bringing widespread rainfall totals ranging
from 2-4". Some highly localized amounts to 6-8" are also possible,
particularly across terrain-favored locations in southwestern Utah,
the Book Cliffs, and Bear River Range.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Mond
weather.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

weather.text:
ESFSLC

The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel will merge with a fall-like
storm system over the western United States, bringing moderate to
heavy rainfall and a resulting threat of flooding. Widespread
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches is expected, locally in excess of 3
inches, particularly across south aspects of southern Utah
mountains, between late Saturday and Monday morning.

Expect many area waterways including streams, rivers, normally
dry washes, creeks, and slot canyons to have rising, fast flows by
Sunday evening. Current forecasts do not bring any rivers to
flood stage, but this will be monitored as the fine details of
heavy rain bands become more confident. Those with activities near
